assumptions.condition: For every \(t\in\mathcal A_T\), the law \(Q_M(t,\cdot)\) is obtained by replacing the rows at vertices in \(T\) by point masses at \(t\) in the product factorization.
For every \(i\in W\) and every \(u\in\mathcal A_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}\), the row \(\theta_i(\cdot\mid u)\) is a point mass at an unknown state of \(\mathcal A_i\).
\(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent draws from the categorical law \(p\).
On the active witness branch, every cell \(p_{zx}\) used as a divisor satisfies \(p_{zx}\ge\epsilon\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal A,V,W,T)\)
definitions.construction: \(\{M=(G,\mathcal A,\theta): P_M\text{ obeys the recursive product factorization},\ Q_M\text{ obeys truncated intervention semantics},\ \theta_i(\cdot\mid u)\text{ is a point mass for }i\in W,\ P_M(T=t)>0\text{ for every }t\in\mathcal A_T\}\).

definitions.name: graphwide \(F\)-identification
definitions.construction: \(q\text{ is graphwide }F\text{-identified}\iff\forall M_1,M_2\in\mathfrak M,\ p_{M_1}=p_{M_2}\Rightarrow q_{M_1}=q_{M_2}\).
inputs: The class \(\mathfrak M\), observed-law map \(p_M\), and target map \(q_M\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sep}}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sep}}=\{(\theta^{(0)},\theta^{(1)}):M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M,\ p_{M_0}=p_{M_1},\ q_{M_0}\ne q_{M_1}\}\), represented by the rational-coefficient polynomial equalities and sign conditions induced by the finite graph, alphabet, functional, and joint-positivity declarations.
inputs: A graph, fixed alphabets, qualitative functional declarations, treatment set, outcome set, and rational-coefficient qualitative constraints.

definitions.name: \(S\)
definitions.construction: \(S=(S_{i,u})_{i\in D,\ u\in\mathcal A_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}}\) with \(\varnothing\ne S_{i,u}\subseteq\mathcal A_i\) and \(S_{i,u}\) singleton for \(i\in W\).
inputs: The graph, alphabet family, and functional-node set.

definitions.name: support-guarded exact algebraic certificate \(C\)
definitions.construction: A finite decision DAG whose guards are rational-coefficient polynomial tests \(g(p)=0\) or \(g(p)>0\). A success leaf either gives rational arithmetic expressions for every coordinate of \(q\), with each denominator \(b(p)\) licensed by ancestor guards whose conjunction entails \(b(p)>0\) on the compatible-model stratum, or gives square-free rational-coefficient polynomial relations \(H_j(p,q_j)=0\) together with Thom encodings and rational isolating data certifying one unique admissible vector \(q\) in \(\prod_t\Delta(\mathcal A_Y)\).
inputs: Observed cells and compatibility constraints induced by the fixed input instance.

definitions.name: exact algebraic separating certificate \(\mathsf{Sep}\)
definitions.construction: Two original-alphabet CPT families \(\theta^{(0)},\theta^{(1)}\) with every entry encoded by an integer minimal polynomial and a rational isolating interval or Thom encoding, accompanied by exact polynomial and sign checks that both tables belong to \(\mathfrak M\), that \(p_{M_0}=p_{M_1}\), and that at least one coordinate satisfies \(q_{M_0}(t,y)\ne q_{M_1}(t,y)\).
inputs: A feasible rational-coefficient qualitative input instance and a failed identification branch.

definitions.name: functional-map feasibility enumerator
definitions.construction: Enumerate the \(F\) tuples of maps \(f_i:\mathcal A_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}\to\mathcal A_i\) for \(i\in W\). For each tuple, scan each of the \(J_T\) assignments \(t\in\mathcal A_T\) and at most \(h\) complete assignments for an extension satisfying every equation \(a_i=f_i(a_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})\). On success, set every nonfunctional conditional row to the uniform distribution. On exhaustion, expand \(P_M(T=t)\) as a sum of nonnegative monomials, record the functional zero factor in every monomial, and combine the resulting identity \(P_M(T=t)=0\) with the positivity encoding \(P_M(T=t)s_t^2=1\).

definitions.name: guarded-district handle for \(\mathsf{F\text{-}ID}^{+}\)
definitions.construction: Start from the exact functional-map feasibility enumerator; refine feasible models by reachable row-support and algebraic strata; propagate denominator licenses bottom-up through sums, products, fractions, marginalization, fixing, and district decomposition; eliminate functional nodes only when their declared alphabets are preserved; encode a successful algebraic leaf by a rational expression or a square-free relation with unique-root Thom data; and turn a terminal failed guarded district into an exact original-alphabet algebraic pair by support-hole row variation or a cardinality-preserving hedge lift. Rational expressions and rational pairs are preferred whenever the stratum admits them.
inputs: The finite instance and the target vector \(q_M\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal I(p)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal I(p_{\mathrm w})=[L_0,L_0+M_0]\times[L_1,L_1+M_1]\), where \(L_x=\sum_{z:p_{zx}>0}p_zp_{\mathrm w}(z,x,Y=1)/p_{zx}\) and \(M_x=\sum_{z:p_z>0,\ p_{zx}=0}p_z\).
inputs: The hidden-functional witness law \(p_{\mathrm w}\) satisfying \(p_{\mathrm w}(X=x)>0\) for \(x\in\{0,1\}\).

definitions.name: \((M^-,M^+)\)
definitions.construction: On \(G_{\mathrm w}\) with the fixed binary alphabets \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm w}\) and the coordinate choices \(V_{\mathrm c}=\{Z,A,X,Y\}\), \(H_{\mathrm c}=W_{\mathrm c}=\varnothing\), \(T_{\mathrm c}=\{Z,X\}\), and \(Y_{\mathrm c}=\{Y\}\), set \(P(Z=1)=\lambda\), \(P(A=1\mid Z=z)=\alpha_z\), and \(P(X=A\mid A)=1\). In both models set \(P(Y=1\mid A=a,X=a)=r_a\). Set both rows \((A,X)=(1,0),(0,1)\) to \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\eta)\) in \(M^-\) and to \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1-\eta)\) in \(M^+\). All unmentioned complementary binary probabilities are fixed by normalization.

definitions.name: \(\widehat q_x\)
definitions.construction: \(\widehat q_x=\sum_{z:\widehat p_{zx}>0}\widehat p_z\,\widehat p(z,x,Y=1)/\widehat p_{zx}\), with an arbitrary bounded value assigned on empirical zero-denominator events that lie outside the active population branch.
inputs: The empirical multinomial law \(\widehat p\) and a fixed treatment value \(x\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\)
definitions.construction: Construct simultaneous two-sided Clopper--Pearson intervals for every observed multinomial cell with individual noncoverage \(\alpha/|\mathcal A_V|\), intersect their Cartesian product with the probability simplex and the feasible observed-law image, and take the union of the target images over every compatible support branch.
inputs: The cell-count vector \(N\), confidence level \(1-\alpha\), and the branchwise target map.

statements.statement: The class \(\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal A,V,W,T)\) is nonempty if and only if some tuple of deterministic maps for \(W\) has, for every \(t\in\mathcal A_T\), a complete assignment extending \(t\) and satisfying all functional equations. The functional-map feasibility enumerator decides this condition in \(O(FJ_T(d+m)h+FR)\) table operations; on feasibility it returns an original-alphabet rational model with uniform nonfunctional rows, and on infeasibility it returns the exact identity \(P_M(T=t)=0\) for a failed assignment \(t\), expanded as functional-zero monomials, together with its contradiction with \(P_M(T=t)s_t^2=1\).
statements.justification: Identification over an empty constrained class is vacuous, so exact fixed-alphabet feasibility must be decided before any causal-effect claim.
statements.gap: Chen and Darwiche give sufficient consistency conditions, while canonical-SCM and arithmetic-circuit papers presuppose or globally optimize over a compatible class; none supplies this fixed-alphabet if-and-only-if certificate with an elementary causal enumeration.
statements.consumer: A constrained extension of the CRAN package dosearch can reject contradictory functional and positivity declarations and return a checkable witness or certificate before formula search.
statements.proof_tex:
For a tuple \(f=(f_i)_{i\in W}\) of deterministic maps and a treatment assignment \(t\in\mathcal A_T\), define
\[
 \Gamma_f(t)
 =\left\{a_D\in\Omega:
 a_T=t\ \text{ and }\
 a_i=f_i(a_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})\ \text{for every }i\in W
 \right\}.
\]
There are exactly
\[
 \prod_{i\in W}
 |\mathcal A_i|^{|\mathcal A_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}|}
 =\prod_{i\in W}|\mathcal A_i|^{r_i}=F
\]
such tuples, by the definitions of \(r_i\) and \(F\).

First suppose that \(M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal A,V,W,T)\).  By qualitative functionality, each functional row selects a unique value, and hence determines one tuple \(f\).  For any \(t\in\mathcal A_T\), causal factorization gives
\[
 P_M(T=t)
 =\sum_{a_{D\setminus T}\in\mathcal A_{D\setminus T}}
   \prod_{i\in D}
   \theta_i(a_i\mid a_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}).
\]
Every summand is nonnegative because every conditional-table entry is a probability.  Joint-treatment positivity says that the left-hand side is strictly positive.  A finite sum of nonnegative numbers is strictly positive only if one summand is strictly positive.  In such a summand every factor at a vertex \(i\in W\) must equal the selected point-mass entry, so
\(a_i=f_i(a_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})\).  Consequently \(\Gamma_f(t)\ne\varnothing\) for every \(t\).

Conversely, suppose that a tuple \(f\) satisfies \(\Gamma_f(t)\ne\varnothing\) for every \(t\).  Define a CPT family \(\theta^f\) by
\[
 \theta^f_i(a\mid u)
 =\begin{cases}
  1, & i\in W\ \text{and }a=f_i(u),\\
  0, & i\in W\ \text{and }a\ne f_i(u),\\
  |\mathcal A_i|^{-1}, & i\notin W.
 \end{cases}
\]
Every row is normalized and nonnegative, every declared functional row is a point mass, and every entry is rational.  Let \(M_f=(G,\mathcal A,\theta^f)\), with the factorization and truncated-intervention semantics stipulated in the model-class definition.  If \(a_D\in\Gamma_f(t)\), then
\[
 P_{M_f}(a_D)
 =\prod_{i\in W}1
  \prod_{i\in D\setminus W}|\mathcal A_i|^{-1}
 >0.
\]
Hence, choosing one \(a_D\in\Gamma_f(t)\),
\[
 P_{M_f}(T=t)
 \ge P_{M_f}(a_D)>0.
\]
This holds for every \(t\), so \(M_f\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal A,V,W,T)\).  This proves both directions and also proves that the feasible witness preserves all prescribed alphabets.

For the operation count, enumerate the \(F\) map tuples.  For a fixed pair \((f,t)\), scan at most \(h=|\Omega|\) complete assignments.  Comparing \(a_T\) with \(t\) costs at most \(d\) operations, and checking all functional equations costs at most one vertex operation per functional vertex plus one parent-coordinate access per incident edge, hence \(O(d+m)\).  The scans therefore cost
\[
 O\!\left(FJ_T(d+m)h\right).
\]
Generating or reading all functional row choices and, on success, writing uniform rows costs at most \(O(FR)\) row operations.  Thus the claimed total is
\[
 O\!\left(FJ_T(d+m)h+FR\right).
\]
All loops range over finite sets, so the enumerator terminates.

It remains to justify the exact infeasibility certificate.  If no tuple succeeds, then for every \(f\) the scan returns an assignment \(t_f\) with \(\Gamma_f(t_f)=\varnothing\).  On the branch selecting \(f\), expand
\[
 P_M(T=t_f)
 =\sum_{a_{D\setminus T}}
   \prod_{i\in D}
   \theta_i(a_i\mid a_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}).
\]
Every extension of \(t_f\) violates at least one functional equation, by emptiness of \(\Gamma_f(t_f)\); the corresponding monomial therefore contains an entry declared zero on that branch.  Thus the displayed network polynomial is identically zero on the branch, with a recorded zero factor for every monomial.

For a single global algebraic check, let
\[
 E_f=\prod_{i\in W}\prod_{u\in
 \mathcal A_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}}
 \theta_i(f_i(u)\mid u).
\]
Point-mass rows obey normalization and the valid orthogonality relations
\[
 \theta_i(a\mid u)\theta_i(b\mid u)=0
 \quad(a\ne b).
\]
Expanding the product of the row normalizations gives the exact identity
\[
 \sum_f E_f
 =\prod_{i\in W}\prod_u\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_i}
   \theta_i(a\mid u)=1.
\]
Because \(\Gamma_f(t_f)=\varnothing\), every monomial of
\(E_fP_M(T=t_f)\) contains two distinct entries from some functional row and is therefore zero by orthogonality.  Hence
\[
 E_fP_M(T=t_f)=0
 \quad\text{for every }f.
\]
Strict positivity of a nonnegative treatment probability is equivalently encoded by the existence of a real auxiliary variable \(s_t\) satisfying
\[
 P_M(T=t)s_t^2=1:
\]
if the probability is positive take \(s_t=P_M(T=t)^{-1/2}\), while the equation and nonnegativity imply strict positivity in the reverse direction.  Multiplying the equation for \(t_f\) by \(E_f\) yields
\[
 E_f=E_fP_M(T=t_f)s_{t_f}^2=0.
\]
Summing over \(f\) contradicts \(\sum_fE_f=1\).  The enumerator can output the finite list \((f,t_f)\), every expanded network monomial with its functional zero factor, the normalization identity, and these displayed polynomial reductions.  They use rational coefficients and constitute the asserted exact infeasibility certificate.

statements.statement: For a fixed row-support pattern \(S\), an observational or interventional cell is strictly positive if and only if at least one compatible complete assignment uses only entries in \(S\) in the corresponding product or truncated product. There are at most \(2^K\) row-support patterns, and every entailed support guard is decidable by finite reachability.
statements.justification: Nonnegative network polynomials convert positivity from an analytic side condition into a finite support-reachability fact.
statements.gap: Hwang et al. propagate sufficient positivity through an already chosen formula; this lemma computes exact row-support consequences before and during formula construction.
statements.consumer: The guard checker in dosearch can attach a finite support witness to every permitted division.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a row-support pattern \(S\).  By its definition,
\[
 \theta_i(a\mid u)>0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 a\in S_{i,u}.
\]
Let \(B\subseteq D\) and fix a cell \(B=b\).  Causal factorization expands its observational probability as
\[
 P_M(B=b)
 =\sum_{a_{D\setminus B}}
   \prod_{i\in D}
   \theta_i(a_i\mid a_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}),
\]
where the sum ranges over complete assignments extending \(b\).  Each product is nonnegative.  A particular product is strictly positive if and only if every one of its finitely many factors is strictly positive, which, by the displayed support equivalence, holds if and only if
\[
 a_i\in S_{i,a_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}}
 \quad\text{for every }i\in D.
\]
A finite sum of nonnegative terms is positive if and only if at least one term is positive.  This proves the observational assertion.

For an intervention \(do(T=t)\), truncated intervention semantics gives, for any cell \(B=b\) disjoint from the fixed intervention coordinates,
\[
 P_M(B=b\mid do(T=t))
 =\sum_{a_{D\setminus(T\cup B)}}
   \prod_{i\in D\setminus T}
   \theta_i(a_i\mid a_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}),
\]
where all summands extend both \(a_T=t\) and \(a_B=b\).  The identical nonnegative-sum argument shows that this cell is positive exactly when one compatible complete assignment uses only supported entries in the truncated product.  No division or limiting argument is used.

For row \((i,u)\), there are \(2^{|\mathcal A_i|}-1\) possible nonempty supports, and functionality restricts a declared functional row to singleton supports.  Ignoring that restriction gives the upper bound
\[
 \prod_{i\in D}
 \left(2^{|\mathcal A_i|}-1\right)^{r_i}
 \le
 \prod_{i\in D}2^{|\mathcal A_i|r_i}
 =2^{\sum_{i\in D}|\mathcal A_i|r_i}
 =2^K.
\]
For a specified observational or interventional cell and a specified \(S\), enumerate the at most \(h\) compatible complete assignments and test the finitely many indicated membership relations.  The preceding equivalences show that this reachability test decides the positivity guard exactly.  Enumerating the at most \(2^K\) strata also decides whether such a guard is entailed on any declared finite collection of compatible support strata.

statements.statement: Let \(M\in\mathfrak M\) contain a parent configuration \(u\) of a nonintervened vertex whose observational probability is zero. If the target coordinate \(q_M(t,y)\) is nonconstant as that conditional row varies over its simplex, then two vertices of that simplex give original-alphabet models \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M\) with \(p_{M_0}=p_{M_1}\) and \(q_{M_0}(t,y)\ne q_{M_1}(t,y)\); rational unchanged rows yield a rational separating pair.
statements.justification: This is the local countermodel compiler for failures caused by structural or sampling-support holes.
statements.gap: Classical hedge witnesses address positive-support latent confounding, while Chen and Darwiche use zero-parent-row changes inside a converse that may enlarge alphabets; this lemma preserves the prescribed alphabets.
statements.consumer: A failed guarded search can return an explicit diagnostic pair rather than the undifferentiated label \(\texttt{nonidentifiable}\).
statements.proof_tex:
Let the row in the statement belong to vertex \(i\notin T\), and write its parent configuration as \(u\).  For \(r\in\Delta(\mathcal A_i)\), let \(M^r\) be obtained from \(M\) by replacing only \(\theta_i(\cdot\mid u)\) by \(r\).  When \(i\in W\), only vertex choices \(r=\delta_a\) are asserted to belong to the qualitative-functional class; when \(i\notin W\), every \(r\) is allowed.

First, the joint law of the parents of \(i\) does not depend on the conditional row of \(i\).  Indeed, no descendant of \(i\) can be a parent of \(i\), by acyclicity.  In the causal product, first sum all descendants of \(i\) in reverse topological order.  Once the descendants of such a vertex have been summed, its own conditional row is the only remaining factor involving its state, so its sum is \(1\).  After all proper descendants have been removed in this way, summing over the state of \(i\) also replaces its conditional row by \(1\).  The remaining finite sum computes the parent marginal and contains no entry from the row at \(i\).  Therefore
\[
 P_{M^r}(\operatorname{pa}_G(i)=u)
 =P_M(\operatorname{pa}_G(i)=u)=0.
\]
All full-assignment probabilities are nonnegative.  Hence every full assignment satisfying \(a_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}=u\) has probability zero under both \(M\) and \(M^r\).  If the parent configuration is different from \(u\), the two causal products use identical rows.  It follows cell by cell that
\[
 P_{M^r}(a_D)=P_M(a_D)
 \quad\text{for every }a_D\in\Omega,
\]
and therefore
\[
 p_{M^r}=p_M.
\]
In particular all treatment marginals are unchanged, so the joint-treatment positivity already possessed by \(M\) is preserved.  Row normalization, nonnegativity, the graph, and the alphabets are also preserved; for vertex choices the functionality declaration is preserved as well.

Because \(i\notin T\), the truncated product for the fixed target coordinate still contains exactly one entry from the row of vertex \(i\).  Grouping the terms according to the value of \(a_i\) when the parents equal \(u\) gives constants \(c\) and \(c_a\), independent of \(r\), such that
\[
 q_{M^r}(t,y)=c+\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_i}c_a r(a).
\]
Thus this coordinate is affine in \(r\).  Since every
\(r\in\Delta(\mathcal A_i)\) has the representation
\[
 r=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_i}r(a)\delta_a,
\]
affineness yields
\[
 q_{M^r}(t,y)
 =\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_i}r(a)
   q_{M^{\delta_a}}(t,y).
\]
If all vertex values on the right were equal, the function would be constant on the simplex.  The assumed nonconstancy therefore supplies \(a_0,a_1\in\mathcal A_i\) with
\[
 q_{M^{\delta_{a_0}}}(t,y)
 \ne q_{M^{\delta_{a_1}}}(t,y).
\]
Set \(M_0=M^{\delta_{a_0}}\) and \(M_1=M^{\delta_{a_1}}\).  The preceding invariance proves \(p_{M_0}=p_{M_1}\), while the last display separates the target coordinate.  Both models use the original alphabets and belong to \(\mathfrak M\).  Finally, if every unchanged row is rational, the only new entries are zeros and ones, so both CPT families are rational.

statements.statement: For every finite graph, fixed-alphabet, qualitative-functional input whose constraints have rational coefficients, if \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sep}}\ne\varnothing\), then \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sep}}\) contains a pair \(M_0,M_1\) all of whose CPT entries lie in the field of real algebraic numbers. Each entry therefore admits an integer minimal polynomial and rational root-isolation or Thom data, and equality of the observed laws and inequality of the intervention vectors admit exact real-closed-field verification.
statements.justification: The transfer principle for real closed fields converts existence of a separator over a rational semialgebraic instance into a finite exact algebraic certificate without claiming a rational witness.
statements.gap: Canonical response-function and polynomial-program representations establish semialgebraicity, but the proposed output contract needs the explicit certificate-level consequence that a nonempty rational separating set has an encodable real-algebraic point.
statements.consumer: The dosearch verifier can check a returned nonidentification pair exactly using minimal polynomials, isolating intervals, and polynomial sign evaluation.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(N\) be the finite number of scalar CPT entries in one copy of the parameterization.  Row nonnegativity and normalization are rational polynomial sign conditions.  For a declared functional row, the point-mass condition is the finite disjunction, over \(a\in\mathcal A_i\), of
\[
 \theta_i(a\mid u)=1,
 \qquad
 \theta_i(b\mid u)=0\quad(b\ne a).
\]
By causal factorization, every observational cell is a finite sum of degree-\(d\) monomials in CPT entries.  By truncated intervention semantics, every target cell is likewise a finite sum of monomials, with factors at \(T\) omitted.  Thus joint-treatment positivity, equality of the two observed laws, and inequality of the two target vectors are all finite Boolean combinations of rational-coefficient polynomial equalities and strict or weak inequalities.  In particular, nonemptiness of \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sep}}\) is the truth over the real numbers of an existential first-order sentence \(\Phi\) in \(2N\) variables with rational coefficients.

The cited Tarski transfer lemma applies because both the real numbers and the field of real algebraic numbers are real closed and \(\Phi\) has only rational coefficients.  Hence
\[
 \mathbb R\models\Phi
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\models\Phi.
\]
Therefore, whenever \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sep}}\ne\varnothing\), it contains a pair whose every CPT entry is real algebraic.  Notice that this is an existence transfer after nonidentification has been established; it does not use quantifier elimination as an identification search.

For each such entry \(\xi\), its monic minimal polynomial over the rationals can be cleared of denominators to obtain a primitive integer polynomial.  Characteristic zero makes that polynomial square-free.  Because it has finitely many real roots and the rationals are dense, rational endpoints can be chosen that isolate \(\xi\) from its other real roots; alternatively, the signs of the successive derivatives give Thom data selecting that root.  The cited exact-encoding lemma then supplies exact arithmetic and sign determination for rational polynomials evaluated at the finite algebraic tuple.  Applying it to the row constraints, the observed-law difference polynomials, and a target-coordinate difference polynomial verifies respectively
\[
 M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M,
 \qquad p_{M_0}=p_{M_1},
 \qquad q_{M_0}\ne q_{M_1}.
\]
These are precisely the membership, equality, and separation checks required by the algebraic separating certificate.

statements.statement: Suppose \(W=\varnothing\) and \(p(v)>0\) for every \(v\in\mathcal A_V\). Whenever \(\mathsf{ID}(G,V,T,Y)\) returns \(\phi_{\mathrm{ID}}(p)\), that functional is constant on every observed-law fiber of the fixed-alphabet class and can be represented by a support-guarded rational success certificate whose denominator guards are entailed by strict observational positivity. This implication is one-way: no converse from fixed-alphabet identification to classical ID is asserted. In the further special case \(H=\varnothing\), the certificate reduces to the ordinary truncated g-formula \(Q_M(t,y)=\sum_{a_{D\setminus(T\cup Y)}}\prod_{i\in D\setminus T}p(a_i\mid a_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})\).
statements.justification: This is the valid sanity collapse: the guarded language contains every classical ID success, while fixed cardinalities are allowed to add identifications that a latent projection cannot see.
statements.gap: Shpitser--Pearl completeness concerns the saturated semi-Markovian model represented by an ADMG; fixed endogenous alphabets define a potentially smaller model class, so only the sound embedding of returned ID functionals transfers without an additional saturation hypothesis.
statements.consumer: A constrained dosearch mode can reuse every formula produced by its classical core and invoke the new search only after classical ID fails.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a strictly positive observed law \(p\), meaning
\[
 p(v)>0\qquad\text{for every }v\in\mathcal A_V,
\]
and suppose \(W=\varnothing\).  Let \(M\in\mathfrak F(p)\).  Causal factorization and truncated intervention semantics make \(M\) a recursive latent-variable causal model compatible with the latent projection of \(G\) onto \(V\).  The cited soundness theorem for \(\mathsf{ID}\) therefore gives, coordinate by coordinate, whenever the algorithm succeeds,
\[
 Q_M(t,y)=\phi_{\mathrm{ID}}(p)(t,y).
\]
Thus, if \(M_1,M_2\in\mathfrak F(p)\),
\[
 q_{M_1}=\phi_{\mathrm{ID}}(p)=q_{M_2}.
\]
This proves constancy on the strictly positive observed-law fiber.  It proves only the stated sound implication from successful classical identification; no failure-to-nonidentification converse is used.

It remains to build the support-guarded representation.  The successful \(\mathsf{ID}\) recursion described in the cited result uses finitely many marginalizations, products, and conditional-probability divisions.  Strict positivity of all joint observed cells implies positivity of every observed marginal, since for \(B\subseteq V\),
\[
 p(B=b)=\sum_{v:v_B=b}p(v)>0.
\]
Starting with the positive cells \(p(v)\), an induction over the successful recursion shows that every kernel entry being normalized is positive: finite products of positive entries are positive, and any nonempty finite marginal sum of positive entries is positive.  Hence each conditional-probability divisor is strictly positive.

For a mechanical polynomial guard trace, place the finitely many rational-coefficient guards
\[
 p(v)>0,\qquad v\in\mathcal A_V,
\]
at the root.  At any later division, clear the already licensed positive denominators from its divisor.  The result is a rational-coefficient polynomial that is a nonempty sum of products of the guarded positive cells, and is therefore strictly positive.  Add that polynomial sign test immediately above the division.  Induction over the finite expression proves that every divisor has an ancestor guard whose conjunction entails its strict positivity.  The resulting finite decision DAG is a support-guarded rational success certificate and returns \(\phi_{\mathrm{ID}}(p)=q_M\).

Finally suppose \(H=\varnothing\), so \(V=D\).  Strict positivity of \(p\) implies \(p(a_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})>0\) for every parent assignment.  Sum the causal product first over the descendants of \(i\) in reverse topological order; row normalization removes all their factors.  The factor at \(i\), which depends only on the retained values of \(i\) and its parents, can then be taken outside the remaining sum over nondescendants.  That remaining sum is the parent marginal, and therefore
\[
 p(a_i,a_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})
 =\theta_i(a_i\mid a_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})
  p(a_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}).
\]
Division is licensed by the positive parent marginal, and hence
\[
 \theta_i(a_i\mid a_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})
 =p(a_i\mid a_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}).
\]
Substituting this equality into the truncated factorization and marginalizing the nonoutcome, nonintervened coordinates proves
\[
 Q_M(t,y)
 =\sum_{a_{D\setminus(T\cup Y)}}
   \prod_{i\in D\setminus T}
   p(a_i\mid a_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}),
\]
with \(a_T=t\) and \(a_Y=y\) in every summand.  Every displayed conditional denominator is again licensed by strict observational positivity.

statements.statement: Can the guarded-district handle be completed into a terminating \(\mathsf{F\text{-}ID}^{+}\) procedure for rational-coefficient qualitative inputs such that every input is first certified feasible or infeasible and every feasible input yields exactly one of the following: a support-guarded exact algebraic certificate \(C\) whose active leaf uniquely certifies \(q_M\) for every \(M\in\mathfrak M\), or an exact algebraic separating certificate \(\mathsf{Sep}\) for two original-alphabet models \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M\) with \(p_{M_0}=p_{M_1}\) and \(q_{M_0}\ne q_{M_1}\)? Guards must be rational-coefficient polynomial sign tests; success leaves may be rational expressions or square-free relations in \(p,q\) with Thom and root-isolation data proving a unique admissible \(q\); failure leaves must encode every CPT entry by an integer minimal polynomial and rational isolating or Thom data and must include exact checks of equal observed laws and unequal targets. The completion must be sound and complete, derive an explicit elementary termination and output-size bound from \(F,J_T,2^K,h,d,m\), use generic real quantifier elimination only to verify returned certificates rather than to search for identification, and embed every successful classical ID output as in the classical-ID embedding proposition without asserting the converse for fixed alphabets. On the overlap of its input language with the finite fixed-alphabet class, this would strictly strengthen only the soundness-only return guarantee of Hwang et al. Theorem 6.1 by adding a total success-or-exact-countermodel guarantee. Relative to Chen--Darwiche Theorem 18 it is a non-comparable fixed-alphabet refinement: joint-treatment positivity implies their separate marginal treatment positivity and is therefore the narrower positivity domain, while preservation of every declared alphabet and a total certificate on both outcomes are orthogonal stronger output requirements.
statements.justification: The alphabet-preserving success-or-countermodel dichotomy is the theorem-level kernel that turns functional knowledge and weak support into a complete decision procedure.
statements.gap: Chen--Darwiche Theorem 18 works on the broader separate-marginal-positivity domain but its converse construction may enlarge a parent alphabet and it does not require a total exact certificate; Hwang et al. prove only soundness when a formula and positivity condition are returned; Chen--Darwiche invariant-cut recognition is complete only under strict positivity.
statements.consumer: The CRAN dosearch engine gains a complete constrained mode whose positive answers are executable exact algebraic certificates and whose negative answers are reproducible original-alphabet algebraic models.

statements.statement: In the fixed binary class \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm w,X}\), where \(A=f(Z)\), suppose \(p_{\mathrm w}(X=x)>0\) for \(x\in\{0,1\}\). The sharp law-specific identified set of \((Q_{X,M}(0,1),Q_{X,M}(1,1))\) is exactly \(\mathcal I(p_{\mathrm w})=[L_0,L_0+M_0]\times[L_1,L_1+M_1]\). Every point of the rectangle is attained by a model using the original binary alphabets, and the vector is point identified if and only if \(p_{zx}>0\) for every \(z\) with \(p_z>0\) and every \(x\in\{0,1\}\).
statements.justification: The rectangle is a nontrivial sharp boundary test that forces the general recursion to distinguish graphwide failure from law-specific identification.
statements.gap: Duarte et al. and Zhang et al. return numerical or polynomial-program characterizations for generic discrete bounds; this result is a closed, support-indexed vector region with simultaneous exact attainability.
statements.consumer: The example becomes a regression test for support-aware formula and countermodel output in dosearch.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix an observed law \(p_{\mathrm w}\) satisfying the hypothesis, and let
\[
\mathcal F(p_{\mathrm w})
=\{M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm w,X}:p_M=p_{\mathrm w}\}
\]
be its model fiber.  We first prove the outer inclusion.  For
\(M\in\mathcal F(p_{\mathrm w})\), qualitative functionality gives a map
\(f:\{0,1\}\to\{0,1\}\) for which
\(\theta_A(a\mid z)=\mathbf 1\{a=f(z)\}\).  Put
\[
\pi_z=\theta_Z(z),\qquad
e_{ax}=\theta_X(x\mid a),\qquad
m_{ax}=\theta_Y(1\mid a,x).
\]
The recursive factorization assumption, applied to the edges of
\(G_{\mathrm w}\), and summation over the hidden value \(A\) give, for every
\(z,x\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
p_z=\pi_z,
\qquad
p_{zx}=\pi_z e_{f(z),x},
\qquad
p_{\mathrm w}(z,x,Y=1)=\pi_z e_{f(z),x}m_{f(z),x}.
\tag{1}
\]
By the truncated-intervention assumption, intervention on \(X\) deletes the
factor \(e_{f(z),x}\), and hence
\[
Q_{X,M}(x,1)=\sum_{z\in\{0,1\}}\pi_zm_{f(z),x}
=\sum_{z\in\{0,1\}}p_zm_{f(z),x}.
\tag{2}
\]
If \(p_{zx}>0\), all factors in the middle identity in (1) are nonnegative,
so \(p_z>0\) and \(e_{f(z),x}>0\); division in the last identity in (1) is
therefore licensed and yields
\[
m_{f(z),x}=\frac{p_{\mathrm w}(z,x,Y=1)}{p_{zx}}.
\tag{3}
\]
If \(p_z>0\) and \(p_{zx}=0\), then (1) instead implies
\(e_{f(z),x}=0\), while the Bernoulli row parameter only satisfies
\(0\le m_{f(z),x}\le1\).  Values with \(p_z=0\) make zero contribution to
(2).  Thus, with
\[
H_x=\{z:p_z>0,\ p_{zx}=0\},
\]
equations (2)--(3) and Definition~\texttt{def:binary-identified-region}
give
\[
Q_{X,M}(x,1)
=L_x+\sum_{z\in H_x}p_zm_{f(z),x},
\qquad
L_x\le Q_{X,M}(x,1)\le L_x+\sum_{z\in H_x}p_z
=L_x+M_x.
\tag{4}
\]
This argument remains valid when two values of \(z\) share the same latent
state: if \(f(z)=f(z')\) and both \(p_z,p_{z'}\) are positive, then (1) shows
that their \(X\)-support indicators agree because they use the same
\(e_{f(z),x}\).  Shared rows can restrict a particular model but cannot
invalidate (4).

We next prove simultaneous attainability and thereby the reverse inclusion.
Fix any
\[
(r_0,r_1)\in[L_0,L_0+M_0]\times[L_1,L_1+M_1],
\qquad
\delta_x=r_x-L_x\in[0,M_x].
\]
Construct a model \(M^*\) on the original four binary variables as follows.
Set
\[
f^*(z)=z,
\qquad
\theta_Z^*(z)=p_z,
\qquad
\theta_A^*(a\mid z)=\mathbf 1\{a=z\}.
\tag{5}
\]
For \(a=z\), define the two rows of \(X\) by
\[
\theta_X^*(x\mid a=z)=
\begin{cases}
p_{zx}/p_z,&p_z>0,\\
1/2,&p_z=0.
\end{cases}
\tag{6}
\]
The division in (6) is guarded by \(p_z>0\); moreover
\(\sum_xp_{zx}=p_z\), so each displayed row is normalized and nonnegative.
For the \(Y\)-rows put
\[
s_{zx}=
\begin{cases}
p_{\mathrm w}(z,x,Y=1)/p_{zx},&p_{zx}>0,\\
\delta_x/M_x,&z\in H_x\text{ and }M_x>0,\\
0,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\qquad
\theta_Y^*(1\mid a=z,x)=s_{zx},
\quad
\theta_Y^*(0\mid a=z,x)=1-s_{zx}.
\tag{7}
\]
Every division in (7) is explicitly guarded.  In its second case,
\(0\le\delta_x/M_x\le1\), so (7) defines Bernoulli rows.

We verify observational equality cell by cell.  If \(p_z=0\), both
\(p_{\mathrm w}(z,x,y)\) and the law induced by (5)--(7) are zero.  If
\(p_z>0\) and \(p_{zx}=0\), equation (6) makes both induced cells with that
\((z,x)\) zero.  Finally, if \(p_{zx}>0\), equations (5)--(7) give
\[
p_z\frac{p_{zx}}{p_z}
\begin{cases}s_{zx},&y=1,\\1-s_{zx},&y=0,
\end{cases}
=p_{\mathrm w}(z,x,y).
\tag{8}
\]
Thus \(p_{M^*}=p_{\mathrm w}\).  The node \(A\) is functional by (5), and
all mechanisms obey the factorization and truncated-intervention semantics
by construction.  Furthermore,
\[
P_{M^*}(X=x)=\sum_zp_{zx}=p_{\mathrm w}(X=x)>0
\]
for both \(x\), so the joint-treatment-positivity assumption is preserved and
\(M^*\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm w,X}\).

Applying (2) to \(M^*\) and using (7), for each \(x\) with \(M_x>0\) we get
\[
Q_{X,M^*}(x,1)
=L_x+\sum_{z\in H_x}p_z\frac{\delta_x}{M_x}
=L_x+\delta_x=r_x.
\tag{9}
\]
If \(M_x=0\), then \(r_x=L_x\) and the same conclusion follows from (4)
with an empty contribution.  The rows indexed by \(x=0\) and \(x=1\) in
(7) are distinct, so the two choices are simultaneous.  Equations (4) and
(9) prove that the identified set is exactly the asserted Cartesian
rectangle and that every point is achieved without alphabet enlargement.

Finally, this rectangle is a singleton exactly when \(M_0=M_1=0\).  Because
the summands in \(M_x=\sum_{z\in H_x}p_z\) are strictly positive on \(H_x\),
\(M_x=0\) holds exactly when \(p_{zx}>0\) for every \(z\) with \(p_z>0\).
Applying this equivalence for both treatment values proves the stated
point-identification criterion.

statements.statement: In the fixed binary class \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm w,ZX}\), where \(A=f(Z)\), suppose \(p_{\mathrm w}(Z=z,X=x)>0\) for all \(z,x\). The full intervention distribution is graphwide identified by \(Q_{ZX,M}(z,x,y)=p_{\mathrm w}(Y=y\mid Z=z,X=x)\) for every \(z,x,y\).
statements.justification: Joint intervention reveals the genuine functional-node identification gain that disappears after an ordinary latent projection.
statements.gap: Joint positivity here implies the separate marginal treatment positivity used by Chen--Darwiche Theorem 18, so this formula is not a positivity-domain extension of that theorem; its role is an explicit fixed-alphabet functional-node reduction that ordinary ID on the projected bow misses.
statements.consumer: A constrained dosearch implementation must return the guarded conditional formula rather than the bow-graph failure produced by its classical core.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix an arbitrary model \(M=(G_{\mathrm w},\mathcal A_{\mathrm w},\theta)\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm w,ZX}\), and write \(p_{\mathrm w}\) for its observed marginal law on \((Z,X,Y)\).  The parent sets in \(G_{\mathrm w}\) are
\[
\operatorname{pa}_{G_{\mathrm w}}(Z)=\varnothing,
\qquad
\operatorname{pa}_{G_{\mathrm w}}(A)=\{Z\},
\qquad
\operatorname{pa}_{G_{\mathrm w}}(X)=\{A\},
\qquad
\operatorname{pa}_{G_{\mathrm w}}(Y)=\{A,X\}.
\]
By Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:qualitative\text{-}functionality}\), for each \(z\in\{0,1\}\) the row \(\theta_A(\cdot\mid z)\) is a point mass.  Hence there is a unique map \(f:\{0,1\}\to\{0,1\}\) such that
\[
\theta_A(a\mid z)=\mathbf 1\{a=f(z)\}
\qquad(a,z\in\{0,1\}).
\]

Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:causal\text{-}factorization}\), specialized to the displayed parent sets, gives, for every \(z,a,x,y\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_M(Z=z,A=a,X=x,Y=y)
&=\theta_Z(z)\theta_A(a\mid z)\theta_X(x\mid a)\theta_Y(y\mid a,x)\\
&=\theta_Z(z)\mathbf 1\{a=f(z)\}\theta_X(x\mid a)\theta_Y(y\mid a,x).
\end{aligned}
\]
Marginalizing the hidden coordinate \(A\) therefore yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
p_{\mathrm w}(z,x,y)
&=\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}P_M(Z=z,A=a,X=x,Y=y)\\
&=\theta_Z(z)\theta_X(x\mid f(z))\theta_Y(y\mid f(z),x).
\end{aligned}
\]
Because every conditional-probability row is normalized, summing this identity over \(y'\in\{0,1\}\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
p_{\mathrm w}(z,x)
&=\sum_{y'\in\{0,1\}}p_{\mathrm w}(z,x,y')\\
&=\theta_Z(z)\theta_X(x\mid f(z))
  \sum_{y'\in\{0,1\}}\theta_Y(y'\mid f(z),x)\\
&=\theta_Z(z)\theta_X(x\mid f(z)).
\end{aligned}
\]
The support premise in the theorem states that this last quantity is strictly positive for every \((z,x)\).  The same guard also follows from Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:joint\text{-}treatment\text{-}positivity}\) after specializing \(T\) to \(T_{ZX}=\{Z,X\}\).  Thus the observable functional
\[
\Phi(p_{\mathrm w})(z,x,y)
:=
\frac{p_{\mathrm w}(z,x,y)}{p_{\mathrm w}(z,x)}
\]
is well defined on every model under consideration.  Dividing the preceding two factorizations, with the strict-support guard just established, gives
\[
\Phi(p_{\mathrm w})(z,x,y)
=\theta_Y(y\mid f(z),x)
=p_{\mathrm w}(Y=y\mid Z=z,X=x).
\]
This defines only an observed-law functional; the next calculation proves that it equals the causal target.

Under \(do(Z=z,X=x)\), Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:truncated\text{-}intervention}\) replaces the rows at \(Z\) and \(X\) by point masses while leaving the mechanisms at \(A\) and \(Y\) unchanged.  Marginalizing the non-outcome coordinate \(A\) in that truncated product gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q_{ZX,M}(z,x,y)
&=\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}\theta_A(a\mid z)\theta_Y(y\mid a,x)\\
&=\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}\mathbf 1\{a=f(z)\}\theta_Y(y\mid a,x)\\
&=\theta_Y(y\mid f(z),x).
\end{aligned}
\]
Combining the last two displays proves, for every \(z,x,y\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
Q_{ZX,M}(z,x,y)
=\Phi(p_{\mathrm w})(z,x,y)
=p_{\mathrm w}(Y=y\mid Z=z,X=x).
\]

Finally, let \(M,M'\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm w,ZX}\) induce the same observed law \(p_{\mathrm w}\).  Applying the established equality to each model gives
\[
Q_{ZX,M}(z,x,y)=\Phi(p_{\mathrm w})(z,x,y)=Q_{ZX,M'}(z,x,y)
\]
for every \(z,x,y\).  Hence the entire joint-intervention distribution is uniquely determined by the observed law, which is precisely graphwide identification in this class.  Every division in the recovery map is licensed by the explicitly proved guard \(p_{\mathrm w}(z,x)>0\).

statements.statement: Under independent multinomial sampling, the confidence map \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) contains the entire true target image \(\{q_M:M\in\mathfrak F(p)\}\) with probability at least \(1-\alpha\). In particular, empirical zero cells are never promoted to structural-zero guards unless every law in the simultaneous cell region has that zero.
statements.justification: Finite-sample validity must respect uncertainty about which support branch is active rather than conditioning on empirical zeros.
statements.gap: Hwang et al. analyze population well-definedness and Jung et al. estimate a fixed formula; neither covers sampling-valid inference after support-dependent formula selection.
statements.consumer: Users of dosearch obtain a conservative confidence object even when sparse cells make the active identification branch uncertain.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathcal I=\mathcal A_V\) be the finite observed-cell set and put \(K=|\mathcal I|\).  Every prescribed alphabet is finite and nonempty, so \(1\leq K<\infty\).  Also put \(\delta=\alpha/K\); the declared range \(0<\alpha<1\) gives \(0<\delta<1\).  For \(v\in\mathcal I\), define
\[
 N_v=\sum_{j=1}^n {\bf 1}\{O_j=v\}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}multinomial\text{-}sampling}\), marginally \(N_v\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,p(v))\).  The counts need not be mutually independent in what follows.

We first verify the finite-sample property of the intervals used in \(\mathrm{def:branch\text{-}confidence\text{-}map}\).  The two-sided Clopper--Pearson interval of individual noncoverage \(\delta\) is the inversion of the two exact one-sided binomial tests with tail levels \(\delta/2\).  Thus, if \(B_r\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,r)\), its acceptance set after observing \(x\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\) is
\[
 I_\delta(x)
 =\left\{r\in[0,1]:
       \Pr(B_r\geq x)\geq\delta/2
       \ \text{and}\ 
       \Pr(B_r\leq x)\geq\delta/2
   \right\}.
\]
This is an interval because the first displayed tail is nondecreasing in \(r\), whereas the second is nonincreasing in \(r\).  We give the coverage argument rather than invoke asymptotics.  Fix \(r\in[0,1]\), let \(B\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,r)\), and set \(g(k)=\Pr(B\geq k)\).  Since \(g\) is nonincreasing in \(k\), the set
\[
 \{k:g(k)<\delta/2\}
\]
is either empty or is \(\{k_0,k_0+1,\ldots,n\}\) for its least element \(k_0\).  In the latter case,
\[
 \Pr\{g(B)<\delta/2\}=\Pr(B\geq k_0)=g(k_0)<\delta/2;
\]
in the former case the probability is zero.  Applying the same argument to the nondecreasing function \(h(k)=\Pr(B\leq k)\), the set \(\{k:h(k)<\delta/2\}\) is either empty or an initial set \(\{0,\ldots,k_1\}\); in the latter case its probability is \(\Pr(B\leq k_1)=h(k_1)<\delta/2\).  Thus
\[
 \Pr\{h(B)<\delta/2\}<\delta/2.
\]
Consequently, by the union bound,
\[
 \Pr_r\{r\notin I_\delta(B)\}
 \leq
 \Pr\{g(B)<\delta/2\}+\Pr\{h(B)<\delta/2\}
 \leq\delta.
\]
The weak final inequality also covers the empty-set cases.  Substituting \(r=p(v)\) and \(B=N_v\) therefore yields
\[
 \Pr_p\{p(v)\notin I_\delta(N_v)\}\leq\delta
 \qquad(v\in\mathcal I).
\]

Let
\[
 \mathcal E_n=\bigcap_{v\in\mathcal I}
 \{p(v)\in I_\delta(N_v)\}.
\]
No independence among the \(N_v\)'s is needed for the Bonferroni bound
\[
 \Pr_p(\mathcal E_n^c)
 \leq\sum_{v\in\mathcal I}
       \Pr_p\{p(v)\notin I_\delta(N_v)\}
 \leq K\delta=\alpha.
\]
Hence \(\Pr_p(\mathcal E_n)\geq1-\alpha\).

Write \(\mathcal R_n\) for the simultaneous cell region after the two intersections prescribed by \(\mathrm{def:branch\text{-}confidence\text{-}map}\):
\[
 \mathcal R_n=
 \left(\prod_{v\in\mathcal I}I_\delta(N_v)\right)
 \cap\Delta(\mathcal I)
 \cap\{p_{M'}:M'\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal A,V,W,T)\}.
\]
If \(\mathfrak F(p)=\varnothing\), then the asserted target image is empty and the desired inclusion is automatic.  Otherwise, take any \(M_0\in\mathfrak F(p)\).  By \(\mathrm{def:observed\text{-}fiber}\), \(p_{M_0}=p\), so \(p\) lies both in the simplex and in the feasible observed-law image.  On \(\mathcal E_n\), it also lies in every cell interval.  Therefore
\[
 p\in\mathcal R_n \qquad\text{on }\mathcal E_n.
\]

For clarity, the support branch of a model \(M'=(G,\mathcal A,\theta')\) is the row-support family
\[
 S(M')=\left(\{a\in\mathcal A_i:\theta'_i(a\mid u)>0\}\right)_{i\in D,\ u\in\mathcal A_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}}
\]
of \(\mathrm{def:support\text{-}stratum}\).  Each row is a probability vector, so every displayed support is nonempty; by qualitative functionality, its support is a singleton when \(i\in W\).  A branch \(S\) is compatible with \(\mathcal R_n\) precisely when there is a model \(M'\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal A,V,W,T)\) such that \(p_{M'}\in\mathcal R_n\) and \(S(M')=S\).  Now fix an arbitrary \(M\in\mathfrak F(p)\).  By \(\mathrm{def:observed\text{-}fiber}\), \(p_M=p\).  On \(\mathcal E_n\), we have proved that \(p\in\mathcal R_n\), and therefore \(S(M)\) is one of the compatible branches whose target images are unioned in \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\).  In particular, \(M\) occurs in the target image attached to its own branch.  The definition of the confidence map therefore gives
\[
 q_M\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}.
\]
The event \(\mathcal E_n\) is common to all \(M\in\mathfrak F(p)\), so the preceding conclusion is simultaneous:
\[
 \{q_M:M\in\mathfrak F(p)\}
 \subseteq\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}
 \qquad\text{on }\mathcal E_n.
\]
Combining this inclusion with \(\Pr_p(\mathcal E_n)\geq1-\alpha\) proves the first assertion.  Notice that no equality between the observed law \(p\) and the causal target \(q_M\) has been assumed: the conclusion follows by retaining the target image of every causal model whose observed law remains in \(\mathcal R_n\).

It remains to verify the stated guard behavior.  If \(N_v=0\), the lower endpoint of \(I_\delta(0)\) is zero and its upper endpoint \(u\) is determined by
\[
 \Pr\{\operatorname{Bin}(n,u)\leq0\}
 =(1-u)^n=\delta/2,
\]
namely
\[
 u=1-(\delta/2)^{1/n}>0,
\]
where \(n\geq1\) and \(0<\delta/2<1\) justify the root and the strict inequality.  Thus an empirical zero does not by itself force the corresponding population cell to vanish.  After intersection with the simplex and the feasible observed-law image, suppose that some \(r\in\mathcal R_n\) has \(r(v)>0\).  Feasibility supplies a model \(M'\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal A,V,W,T)\) with \(p_{M'}=r\).  Its branch \(S(M')\) is compatible and is retained in the defining union for \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\), while the observed-cell guard \(p_{M'}(v)=0\) is false on that retained branch.  Hence a structural-zero guard for cell \(v\) can hold across the confidence map only if
\[
 \forall r\in\mathcal R_n,\qquad r(v)=0.
\]
This is exactly the second assertion.  The argument uses neither division by an observed cell probability nor a limiting operation, so it requires no additional support, rank, overlap, boundary, or regularity condition beyond the stated finiteness, \(n\geq1\), and \(0<\alpha<1\).

statements.statement: For the point-identified branch of \(G_{\mathrm w}\), if every active \(p_{zx}\ge\epsilon\), then \(\sqrt n(\widehat q-q)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,J\Sigma(p)J^{\mathsf T})\), where \(J\) is the Jacobian of the guarded standardization circuit on that fixed support face. The plug-in covariance is consistent, and every contrast with positive limiting variance has asymptotically exact Wald coverage \(1-\alpha\).
statements.justification: On stable support faces the piecewise problem must collapse to ordinary smooth multinomial inference with no nonregularity tax.
statements.gap: DML-ID supplies asymptotic normality for fixed identifying functionals, while the proposed result derives the exact multinomial collapse for a support-selected branch and pairs it with the branch-respecting procedure at the boundary.
statements.consumer: Applied users receive standard errors and familiar Wald intervals whenever the data-generating support is separated from a guard switch.
statements.proof_tex:
Write
\[
q=\bigl(Q_{X,M}(0,1),Q_{X,M}(1,1)\bigr)^{\mathsf T},
\qquad
\widehat q=(\widehat q_0,\widehat q_1)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Let the eight observed cells be indexed by \(v=(z,x,y)\), and define the
indicator vector \(R_k=(\mathbf 1\{O_k=v\})_v\).  By the independent
multinomial-sampling assumption,
\[
\widehat p=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^nR_k,
\qquad
\mathbb E[R_k]=p,
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}(R_k)=\operatorname{diag}(p)-pp^{\mathsf T}=\Sigma(p).
\tag{10}
\]
The vectors are bounded and hence have finite second moments.  Applying
Lemma~\texttt{lem:multivariate-central-limit} to (10) yields
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat p-p)\Rightarrow
\mathcal N\bigl(0,\Sigma(p)\bigr).
\tag{11}
\]

Let \(S=\{z:p_z>0\}\).  On the point-identified branch,
Theorem~\texttt{thm:binary-rectangle} implies
\(p_{zx}>0\) for every \(z\in S\) and \(x\in\{0,1\}\); the fixed-support
margin strengthens these inequalities to \(p_{zx}\ge\epsilon\).  For a
real cell vector \(r=(r_{zxy})\), write
\(r_z=\sum_{x,y}r_{zxy}\), \(r_{zx}=\sum_yr_{zxy}\), and define, on
\[
\mathcal U=\{r:r_{zx}>\epsilon/2
\text{ for all }z\in S,\ x\in\{0,1\}\},
\]
the guarded standardization map
\[
g_x(r)=\sum_{z\in S}r_z\frac{r_{zx1}}{r_{zx}},
\qquad
g(r)=(g_0(r),g_1(r))^{\mathsf T}.
\tag{12}
\]
Every denominator in (12) is positive on \(\mathcal U\), so \(g\) is a
rational, continuously differentiable map there.  Theorem
\texttt{thm:binary-rectangle} gives \(g(p)=q\).  Its ambient Jacobian
\(J=Dg(p)\) is computable cell by cell: with
\(m_{ax}=p_{ax1}/p_{ax}\),
\[
J_{x,(a,b,c)}
=\mathbf 1\{a\in S\}
\left[
m_{ax}
+\mathbf 1\{b=x\}p_a
\frac{\mathbf 1\{c=1\}p_{ax}-p_{ax1}}{p_{ax}^2}
\right].
\tag{13}
\]
The guards \(p_{ax}\ge\epsilon\) justify both divisions in (13).

For completeness, \(\widehat p\to p\) in probability follows directly from
the sampling assumption: each cell frequency has variance at most \(1/(4n)\),
so Chebyshev's inequality followed by a union bound over eight cells makes
\(\max_v|\widehat p_v-p_v|\to0\) in probability.  Hence
\(P(\widehat p\in\mathcal U)\to1\).  If \(z\notin S\), then \(P(Z=z)=0\),
so its empirical cells are zero almost surely.  Consequently, on
\(\{\widehat p\in\mathcal U\}\), Definition
\texttt{def:binary-estimator} agrees exactly with (12):
\[
\widehat q=g(\widehat p).
\tag{14}
\]
The arbitrary bounded convention on the complementary zero-denominator
event is therefore used with probability tending to zero.

Apply Lemma~\texttt{lem:finite-dimensional-delta-method} to (11)--(12).
Together with (14), which can alter expectations of a bounded continuous
test function by at most twice its supremum times
\(P(\widehat p\notin\mathcal U)\), this gives
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat q-q)
\Rightarrow
\mathcal N\bigl(0,J\Sigma(p)J^{\mathsf T}\bigr).
\tag{15}
\]

To make the covariance assertion explicit, let \(J(r)=Dg(r)\) on
\(\mathcal U\), and define the plug-in matrix
\[
\widehat V=J(\widehat p)\Sigma(\widehat p)J(\widehat p)^{\mathsf T}
\tag{16}
\]
there, and set \(\widehat V=0\) off \(\mathcal U\).  Both \(J(r)\) and
\(\Sigma(r)=\operatorname{diag}(r)-rr^{\mathsf T}\) are continuous at
\(p\).  The elementary epsilon--delta definition of continuity and
\(\widehat p\to p\), together with
\(P(\widehat p\in\mathcal U)\to1\), therefore imply
\[
\widehat V\mathrel{\mathop{\longrightarrow}^{p}}
V:=J\Sigma(p)J^{\mathsf T}.
\tag{17}
\]

Finally fix any nonrandom contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^2\) whose limiting
variance \(\sigma_c^2=c^{\mathsf T}Vc\) is strictly positive.  By (17),
\(\widehat\sigma_c^2=c^{\mathsf T}\widehat Vc\to_p\sigma_c^2\), so its
nonnegative square root is also consistent and is positive with probability
tending to one.  Lemma~\texttt{lem:studentized-wald-coverage}, applied to
(15) and (17), gives
\[
\frac{\sqrt n\,c^{\mathsf T}(\widehat q-q)}{\widehat\sigma_c}
\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\tag{18}
\]
If \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\) is the \((1-\alpha/2)\)-quantile of the standard
normal law, its continuity and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) yield
\[
P\!\left(
c^{\mathsf T}q\in
\left[c^{\mathsf T}\widehat q
\mathbin{-}z_{1-\alpha/2}\frac{\widehat\sigma_c}{\sqrt n},
c^{\mathsf T}\widehat q
\mathbin{+}z_{1-\alpha/2}\frac{\widehat\sigma_c}{\sqrt n}
\right]
\right)\longrightarrow1-\alpha.
\tag{19}
\]
The strict inequality \(\sigma_c^2>0\) is exactly the nondegeneracy
condition required for the division in (18); no Wald assertion is made for
a zero-variance contrast.

\]

statements.statement:
Let \(\phi:D_\phi\subseteq\mathbb R^k\to\mathbb R^m\) be differentiable at
\(\vartheta\), let \(T_N\) take values in \(D_\phi\), and let
\(r_N\to\infty\).  If \(r_N(T_N-\vartheta)\Rightarrow T\), then
\[
r_N\bigl(\phi(T_N)-\phi(\vartheta)\bigr)
\Rightarrow D\phi(\vartheta)T,
\]
and the difference between the left side and
\(D\phi(\vartheta)r_N(T_N-\vartheta)\) converges to zero in probability.

statements.statement:
Suppose that
\(\sqrt N(T_N-\vartheta)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\) with
\(\sigma>0\), and that \(S_N\to_p\sigma\).  Then
\(\sqrt N(T_N-\vartheta)/S_N\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\), and the
two-sided interval
\[
\left[T_N-z_{1-\alpha/2}S_N/\sqrt N,
T_N+z_{1-\alpha/2}S_N/\sqrt N\right]
\]
has limiting coverage \(1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from the observed categorical law \(p\); no intervention data are sampled.
sampling_model.units: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent observations in the fixed finite space \(\mathcal A_V\).
sampling_model.treatment: The identification model imposes joint positivity \(p(T=t)>0\) for every joint treatment assignment; it does not impose strict positivity on all observed cells.
sampling_model.overlap: Regular Wald inference is restricted to a fixed support face with every active denominator at least \(\epsilon>0\); the confidence-map result allows guard uncertainty.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nonparametric nuisance fitting is required for the finite-alphabet multinomial plug-in; the covariance uses the empirical multinomial law and the active circuit Jacobian.

estimand_functional: \(q\) is the unique admissible root certified by the active leaf \(C(p,q)\), with rational \(q=C(p)\) as the preferred special case and every division licensed by an entailed strict-support guard

tldr: Functional restrictions can identify effects that classical graphical algorithms miss, but they also create structural zeros and algebraic fibers that defeat an exclusively rational output language. The project seeks a complete fixed-alphabet procedure that first certifies consistency, then either returns a branchwise exact algebraic identifying certificate with mechanically justified support guards or returns two exactly encoded real-algebraic models with the same observed law and different full intervention distributions. The construction embeds every sound classical ID success without claiming the false fixed-cardinality converse, is stress-tested on a fully specified binary non-root functional-node instance, and supports multinomial inference that respects uncertainty about the active support branch while reducing to ordinary Wald inference on stable faces.

project_justification.gap: Chen--Darwiche Theorem 18 gives a reduction on the broader separate-marginal-positivity domain, but its converse construction may enlarge alphabets and does not impose a total exact output contract; Hwang et al. extract sufficient positivity for returned formulas but prove only soundness of that return guarantee; classical ID, invariant-cut search, and CSI algorithms do not deliver a fixed-alphabet joint-positive success-or-countermodel dichotomy.
project_justification.niche: Finite alphabets make functional maps and row supports enumerable, while nonnegative network polynomials make support consequences combinatorial; this creates room for a causal-structural algorithm stronger than post-hoc guard extraction but more informative than generic real quantifier elimination.
project_justification.fill: The proposed \(\mathsf{F\text{-}ID}^{+}\) architecture combines exact feasibility, reachable-support and algebraic stratification, guarded district recursion, and alphabet-preserving algebraic countermodel compilation, with rational certificates as a preferred special case, a sharp binary boundary theorem, and branch-respecting multinomial inference.

related_work: Chen and Darwiche (2024, Theorem 18 and its proof in Appendix C) supply the closest identification architecture: close observed-parent functional nodes, eliminate them, and transport same-law models. Positivity of every joint treatment assignment implies their separate marginal treatment positivity, so the present domain is narrower rather than an extension; fixed-alphabet preservation and a total success-or-exact-countermodel certificate are orthogonal output refinements, and the comparison is non-comparable overall because their last transport step may form a Cartesian-product parent state. Hwang et al. (2024, Theorem 5.1, Algorithms 1--2, and Theorem 6.1) provide the denominator-licensing calculus adapted here; on the common finite fixed-alphabet input scope, the proposed total dichotomy strictly strengthens only their soundness-when-returned guarantee by making every failure produce an exact pair. Shpitser and Pearl (2006) provide the classical ID algorithm and hedge completeness for saturated semi-Markovian models; the present fixed-alphabet class inherits every returned ID functional but need not inherit the converse. Chen and Darwiche (2025, Proposition 4 and Section 5) characterize identification through invariant cuts and state that complete cut discovery beyond strict positivity is outside their result, so that work informs rather than supplies the proposed recognizer. Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen (2019, Theorem 1) show the computational hardness of general CSI and give a sound state calculus; Mokhtarian et al. (2022, Theorem 2 and Corollary 1) obtain completeness only by decomposing over observed root-control contexts. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (2022, Theorem 1) and Duarte et al. (2024, Theorem 1 and the district simplification in Proposition 3) supply finite response-function and polynomial-program representations, but not symbolic guarded exact point-identification certificates. Basu, Pollack, and Roy (2006, Chapters 2 and 10) provide the real-closed-field and Thom-encoding machinery used to make algebraic outputs finite and exactly checkable. Jung, Tian, and Bareinboim (2021, Theorems 1--3) provide the fixed-functional estimation comparator; the present inference problem includes random support-branch selection.
technical_internal_limitation: A fiber inside one deterministic-map stratum can contain no rational point, so rational density of ambient CPT simplexes does not imply a rational identifying expression or rational separating pair. For rational-coefficient qualitative input, real-closed-field transfer yields real-algebraic witnesses and the output language encodes them exactly; it does not assert universal rationality. If an externally fixed observed law is transcendental, or numerical constraints have arbitrary real coefficients, the corresponding existence statement is only over the real closure of that coefficient field and need not admit an integer-minimal-polynomial encoding over \(\mathbb Q\). The separately defined unrestricted observed-closure class \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm c}\) and pair \((M^-,M^+)\) are an internal regression test, not a theorem-level comparison with a published reduction. Direct substitution gives \(p_{\mathrm c,M^-}=p_{\mathrm c,M^+}\); every cell \(p_{\mathrm c}(z,a,a,y)\) is positive, \(p_{\mathrm c}(z,x)>0\) for all \(z,x\), and cells with \(x\ne a\) are zero. Thus the common law is relative-interior and nondegenerate on its structural-support face, not full-support. The exact target differences are \(Q_{\mathrm c,M^+}(z,0,1)-Q_{\mathrm c,M^-}(z,0,1)=\alpha_z(1-2\eta)\) and \(Q_{\mathrm c,M^+}(z,1,1)-Q_{\mathrm c,M^-}(z,1,1)=(1-\alpha_z)(1-2\eta)\).
honest_scope: The feasibility theorem, support propagation, support-hole separator, real-algebraic witness lemma, one-way classical ID embedding, binary rectangle, binary joint-intervention formula, and multinomial inference claims are concrete theorem targets. The observed-closure pair is retained only as an internal regression test against an invalid proof move and is not positioned as a refutation of Chen--Darwiche or another published method. The genuinely open content is the cardinality-preserving guarded-district dichotomy: it must cover positive-support hedge failures and algebraic strata without importing generic quantifier elimination as the identification search. The Chen--Darwiche comparison is a non-comparable fixed-alphabet complement because joint positivity is stronger than their separate marginal positivity, whereas alphabet preservation and total exact certificates strengthen the output contract. With \(W=\varnothing\) and strict observational positivity, every successful classical ID functional embeds as a guarded success leaf; no converse is claimed because fixed cardinalities can remove effective confounding. With \(H=\varnothing\), this embedding collapses explicitly to the truncated g-formula. On the hidden-functional binary witness, the procedure must return the sharp single-\(X\) rectangle and identify joint \(Z,X\); the fully specified unrestricted closure pair must remain a failing regression test without any claim of full support away from \(X=A\).
